title: Proof manifest
description: Declares which code, model, encoding and tooling a `proven` or `model-checked` claim depends on, so a diff can decide which proofs must be re-run (V2-29). The manifest is the claim's scope: a dependency it omits is invisible to tools/proof_plan.py. An entry without declared assumptions is rejected by the loader, because a proof whose assumptions are unstated is an overclaim.

version.description: Manifest format version. tools/proof_plan.py rejects anything else.

proofs.description: One entry per proof or bounded model check. An empty list is allowed: a repository with no proofs says so instead of omitting the file.

id.description: Stable proof ID, unique within the manifest.

claim.description: Claim the proof supports. Status lives in the claim ledger, not here.

artifact.description: Model or proof script, relative to --repo (or absolute). It must exist; a manifest that points at nothing is a broken manifest, not a stale proof.

tool_output.description: JSON record of the run, shaped by schemas/tool-output.schema.json (tools/bounded_check.py writes one). Only `status` and `finished_at` are read by the planner; `claim_lint` verifies the hash.

depends_on.description: Code paths or globs the proof abstracts. A changed, renamed or deleted match triggers a re-run. `*` stays within one path segment; `**` crosses segments.

model.description: Additional model files (helpers, imported modules) beyond `artifact`.

encoding.description: Encoding, configuration or harness files whose change can change what the proof means.

tooling.description: Checker wrapper, extractor or translator paths. A change here invalidates the proof even when the model and code stay put.

assumptions.description: What the model abstracts or ignores. Required: a proof without declared assumptions is a status overclaim.

proven_commit.description: Commit the record was produced at. Informational; freshness is decided from `finished_at` and the diff, not from this field.

proven_at.description: Date of the recorded run. Informational.

owner.description: Who decides whether a re-run failure is a model bug or a code bug.

note.description: Free-form note, e.g. why a dependency is listed.
